title: siuba SQL semi-join repeats a left row for duplicate matches
evidence: The SQLAlchemy-backed semi_join selected only left columns from an inner join, so duplicate keys on the right duplicated left rows. The fix uses correlated EXISTS and includes a regression test with two right records for one key.
adaptation: The replay translates the SQLAlchemy construction to an inner join and the upstream correlated EXISTS, keeping the duplicate-key case from the regression test. It replaces ORM-generated aliases, selects a stable synthetic row ID, and omits unused dataframe columns.
before_sql: SELECT l.id FROM lhs l INNER JOIN rhs r ON l.ii = r.ii
after_sql: SELECT l.id FROM lhs l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rhs r WHERE l.ii = r.ii)
